subject: Insurance
title: The Art World's Fire Problem
description: Learn The Art World's Fire Problem in one minute.

hook.text: Insuring art creates a perverse incentive. A painting worth $100,000 on the market might be insured for $500,000.

buildup.text: Art valuation is subjective. Owners inflate values on insurance applications.

discovery.text: Investigators found that some 'destroyed' artwork was actually hidden.

twist.text: In 2001, a collector insured prints for $12 million, then claimed they burned. The prints were found in a storage unit.

climax.text: Art insurance fraud thrives on subjectivity. When value is in the eye of the beholder, so is the motive for destruction.

punchline.text: Insured for $12 million, hidden in storage.

quiz.question: Why is art insurance particularly vulnerable to fraud?
options: Subjective valuations allow owners to inflate coverage
